quiz.title: CBSE Class 12 Maths 2001 Paper Quiz
quiz.intro: Eight board-level questions in the style of the 2001 paper, spanning calculus, matrices, vectors, 3D geometry and probability. Choose an answer for each, then press Check my score.

questions.q: If A is a 3×3 matrix with |A| = 4, what is |2A|?
questions.explanation: For an n×n matrix, |kA| = k<sup>n</sup>|A|. Here n = 3, so |2A| = 2<sup>3</sup> × 4 = 8 × 4 = 32.

questions.q: If y = x<sup>x</sup>, then dy/dx equals:
questions.explanation: Take logs: ln y = x ln x. Differentiate: (1/y) y' = ln x + 1, so dy/dx = x<sup>x</sup>(1 + ln x).

questions.q: Evaluate ∫ from 0 to 1 of x e<sup>x</sup> dx.
questions.explanation: By parts, ∫ x e<sup>x</sup> dx = x e<sup>x</sup> − e<sup>x</sup>. At the limits: (e − e) − (0 − 1) = 1.

questions.q: Two vectors a and b satisfy a · b = |a||b|/2. The angle between them is:
questions.explanation: a · b = |a||b| cosθ, so cosθ = 1/2, giving θ = 60°.

questions.q: A bag has 3 red and 2 black balls. Two are drawn without replacement. What is P(both red)?
A line has direction ratios 2, −1, 2. Its direction cosines are:
questions.explanation: Magnitude = √(4 + 1 + 4) = 3. Divide each ratio by 3 to get (2/3, −1/3, 2/3).

questions.q: For a 3×3 matrix A with |A| = 5, the value of |adj A| is:
The order and degree of (d<sup>2</sup>y/dx<sup>2</sup>)<sup>3</sup> + (dy/dx)<sup>2</sup> + y = 0 are:
questions.explanation: The highest derivative is d<sup>2</sup>y/dx<sup>2</sup> (order 2), and its highest power in the polynomial form is 3 (degree 3).

faq.q: What topics does the CBSE Class 12 Maths 2001 paper cover?
faq.a: It spans the full Class 12 syllabus of that year — differentiation and integration, matrices and determinants, vectors and three-dimensional geometry, differential equations and probability. The mix mirrors what still appears on the board paper today.

faq.q: Are older papers like 2001 still useful for current board exams?
faq.a: Yes. The core concepts — continuity, definite integrals, adjoint and inverse, dot and cross products, conditional probability — have barely changed. Older papers give clean, well-set questions for building fundamentals before you move to recent patterns.

faq.q: How should I use a previous-year paper while revising?
faq.a: Attempt it in one timed sitting without notes, mark it against the answer key, then re-work only the questions you missed. That gap analysis is far more useful than passively reading solved answers.

faq.q: How is the degree of a differential equation decided?
faq.a: First write the equation as a polynomial in its derivatives (no radicals or fractions of derivatives). The degree is then the highest power of the highest-order derivative. If it cannot be written as such a polynomial, the degree is not defined.
